results.notes: Both motors positive and similar, robot moves forward in straight line (y stays at 0.00)
Right motor consistently > Left motor (R-L diff = +0.33). Robot curves left (y increases from 0.00 to 0.06). Strong turn signal at steps 10-20 with L as low as -0.12 and R at 0.85

CRITICAL BUG: Right motor > Left motor (R-L diff = +0.34), causing LEFT turn instead of right. Robot curves LEFT (y increases to 0.05) - identical pattern to 'turn left' instruction. Model cannot differentiate turn directions.

Interesting: Left motor > Right motor (L-R diff = +0.21), causing slight RIGHT curve (y goes negative). This is the ONLY instruction that produces right-turning behavior! Robot moves slowly toward target area. Red ball was at [1.5, 0.5, 0.1] - unclear if visually grounded or just learned behavior.

working_well: Forward motion: Both motors activate with similar values, straight trajectory
Turn left: Strong differential (R > L), clear leftward curve in trajectory
issues: Turn right: Model outputs SAME pattern as turn left (R > L instead of L > R)
Turn right trajectory is nearly identical to turn left trajectory
Visual grounding unclear - 'red ball' instruction produces right turn but may not be visually driven
interesting_observations: Only 'go towards red ball' produces L > R (right-turning) behavior
Turn instructions show strong signals (L going negative at steps 15-20)
Model has learned turning behavior but not direction differentiation
recommendations: Collect explicit 'turn right' training data with L > R motor patterns
Verify training data distribution - may have imbalanced left/right examples
Consider data augmentation: mirror left turn examples to create right turns
Add more visual grounding examples with varied target positions
